title: Published 2.4.3 target retained the 2.4.2 receiver pin
expected_behavior: The adapter selected by ai-sdlc-v2.4.3 calls the ai-sdlc-v2.4.3 result receiver before REAL approval.
observed_behavior: SIM passed but deployed REAL preflight run 35640134916 rejected codex-adapter-v2.4.3 because codex-execute.yml still called ai-sdlc-v2.4.2.
root_cause: The 2.4.3 target tag advanced the production authentication repair without atomically advancing or asserting the target receiver pin; target compatibility accepted any structurally compatible immutable receiver.
evidence: The immutable tagged workflow contains the 2.4.2 receiver reference; REAL preflight expected exactly one 2.4.3 receiver reference and failed before real effects. The republished target tag points at 050dc7bb and calls the 2.4.3 receiver. REAL #150 reached Codex and projected the result through that receiver; its separate sandbox failure is DEF-0043.
resolution: PR #61 repinned the target receiver. The reviewed target tag was replaced at 050dc7bb, the control-plane 2.4.3 tag was rebound and attested via PRs #73/#74, and REAL #150 proved receiver delivery. The exceptional rewrite authorization is complete; future repairs require a new immutable patch release.
notes: High severity because portfolio main already consumed ai-sdlc-v2.4.3, but preflight failed closed before Codex or repository mutation. The 2.4.2 compatibility unit remains the rollback baseline. This receiver mismatch is resolved, but REAL implementation remains blocked by the separate sandbox regression DEF-0043; no blanket production-readiness claim.

title: Repaired adapter was merged but production remained pinned to the pre-repair immutable release
expected_behavior: After a production adapter repair is reviewed and merged, REAL execution selects that repaired code only after a new immutable adapter tag is published, bound in the control-plane registry/runtime record, and release-aware verification passes.
observed_behavior: Portfolio issue #145 routed successfully, but the enabled runtime still resolved consulting-playbook to codex-adapter-v2.4.1 at f34ceacc; that stale adapter launched gpt-5.1-codex and failed with 401 Unauthorized before branch creation, validation, tests, or draft-PR publication even though PR #51 had already merged the repaired gpt-5.3-codex authentication path to main.
root_cause: The production repair was completed at the target repository source level but the immutable adapter release and control-plane repin sequence was not completed before the next governed delivery was approved.
evidence: Issue #145 receiver-validated result recorded execution_status failed, branch_name null, pull_request_url null, validation/test not-run; target logs show checkout of codex-adapter-v2.4.1 at f34ceacc and gpt-5.1-codex before 401; current .github registry/runtime still bind v2.4.1 while PR #51 repair exists only on main. Published 2.4.5 composition selected codex-adapter-v2.4.5 at 4f062ca73acfc3458f0d690bf1c7687bafd0a8eb; REAL #154 completed successfully and produced merged PR #66.
resolution: Resolved: the repaired adapter is published and selected by the immutable 2.4.5 runtime composition, the portfolio consumer advanced only after release/preflight gates, and fresh governed REAL #154 succeeded.
notes: The original 2.4.2-specific repair sequence was superseded by later immutable patch releases; the required lifecycle invariant is now proven by 2.4.5.

title: Production adapter did not reproduce the verified Codex authentication boundary
expected_behavior: Production execution uses the preflight-proven client model and stdin login flow with isolated authentication state; the raw key is absent from executor commands; repository workspace sandbox and publication readiness are explicit before Codex runs.
observed_behavior: The successful preflight logged in to an isolated CODEX_HOME then removed the raw key before its probe; the production adapter instead passed OPENAI_API_KEY and ambient CODEX_* configuration directly to codex exec and did not check publication write access before invoking Codex.
root_cause: The preflight evolved independently after the production adapter was implemented and their runtime boundaries were never reconciled.
evidence: Successful preflight run 34929448831 compared with scripts/codex_target_adapter.py at 857ed6b; ai-sdlc/engineering-journal/2026-09-15-production-adapter-preflight-parity.md. Fresh governed REAL #154 used the published 2.4.5 adapter; run 36279165335 prepared the sandbox, invoked Codex, passed validation/tests, published one managed draft PR, and delivered an accepted canonical result. PR #66 merged after conformance and human review.
resolution: Resolved: the production adapter now reproduces the verified authentication boundary and fresh governed REAL #154 created a tested draft PR with an accepted result through the published 2.4.5 path.
notes: Live draft publication supplies the final permission evidence that a read-only metadata probe cannot establish.

title: Codex preflight discarded actionable failure diagnostics
expected_behavior: Preflight preserves the failing stage and original exit code with safe diagnostic hints.
observed_behavior: The first preflight reported only codex-runtime and deleted combined login/probe output.
root_cause: The workflow collapsed both stages and static tests did not execute failure paths.
evidence: ai-sdlc/engineering-journal/2026-09-13-preflight-diagnostic-gap.md PR #48 merged the staged diagnostic repair and controlled preflight run 34929448831 completed successfully on that repaired workflow.
resolution: Resolved: staged login/probe diagnostics, original exit-code handling, safe hints, and executable failure-path coverage merged in PR #48 and were followed by successful controlled preflight run 34929448831.
notes: The diagnostic defect is closed independently of any historical provider failure.

title: Codex credential readiness lacked a live provider preflight
expected_behavior: Before an approved delivery consumes its identity and execution budget, an operator can run a controlled provider-backed preflight using the protected target environment and exact pinned Codex client without repository or publication effects.
observed_behavior: Offline conformance and secret-presence checks were green, but issue #139 and retry issue #144 both reached the live Codex runtime and failed with 401 Unauthorized before making changes, running validation, or creating a draft pull request.
root_cause: Acceptance coverage deliberately kept ordinary CI offline but supplied no separate live credential-readiness gate, so secret presence was treated as stronger evidence than provider acceptance.
evidence: The target environment resolved OPENAI_API_KEY, then the pinned Codex client exhausted its retries with 401 Unauthorized; the terminal result recorded execution_status failed and validation/test not-run. Controlled Codex authentication preflight run 34929448831 completed successfully on the merged manual protected-environment workflow using the pinned client/model.
resolution: Resolved: the manual environment-gated Codex authentication preflight is merged and controlled run 34929448831 passed, establishing the intended time-specific credential/client/provider readiness claim.
notes: Closure does not claim production readiness; the preflight remains a narrow time-specific provider-readiness gate.

title: Approved issue could dispatch Codex more than once
expected_behavior: One explicit approval action starts one logical authorized execution.
observed_behavior: Multiple labeled events could route the same approved issue before queued state was applied.
root_cause: Routing evaluated the current label snapshot instead of requiring the triggering label to be status:approved.
evidence: Issue #55 documents the remaining duplicate-routing defect and required event-specific guard.
resolution: Require the triggering approval label and reject queued/later states; preserve duplicate delivery as a no-op.
notes: High severity because duplicate dispatch can cause repeated paid AI execution and duplicate mutation attempts.

title: Executor lacked first-class idempotent draft-PR reuse
expected_behavior: Retries of the same logical delivery reuse the owned draft PR without rerunning Codex or publishing again.
observed_behavior: Router protections alone did not prevent replayed canonical inputs from rerunning Codex; existing branch/PR state was not a first-class successful outcome.
root_cause: Publication ownership and replay reconciliation were incomplete at the executor boundary.
evidence: Issue #74 records the missing preflight and required deterministic PR reuse behavior.
resolution: Add deterministic executor preflight and safe reuse/fail-closed handling for existing managed state.
notes: Defense-in-depth defect distinct from source duplicate routing.

title: Non-Slugger portfolio work was mirrored into Slugger
expected_behavior: Portfolio Tasks is the authoritative backlog and direct routing sends work only to the declared target.
observed_behavior: Historical synchronization mirrored general portfolio work into Slugger even when another repository was the target, creating duplicate lifecycle state.
root_cause: Legacy synchronization treated Slugger as a general mirror rather than a bounded target/product owner.
evidence: Issue #75 explicitly documents duplicate lifecycle state caused by non-Slugger mirroring.
resolution: Restrict synchronization to Slugger and registered Slugger-managed outputs; preserve history without duplicate active state.

title: Shared router and contract consumers used mutable references
expected_behavior: Cross-repository contract and router compatibility is bound to an immutable reviewed release.
observed_behavior: Target repositories could consume reusable workflows or contracts from mutable branch references such as @main.
root_cause: The organization lacked one coherent immutable release and consumer pinning policy.
evidence: Issue #76 states mutable references could let unreviewed upstream changes break multiple repositories simultaneously.
resolution: Create coherent versioned release/rollback policy and migrate supported consumers to immutable refs.
notes: High severity due to organization-wide blast radius.

title: Slugger reusable workflow inherited broader secrets than required
expected_behavior: Reusable workflows receive only explicitly named secrets required by their contract.
observed_behavior: At least one supported Slugger reusable workflow call used broad secret inheritance.
root_cause: Caller secret boundary was broader than the least-privilege workflow contract.
evidence: Issue #77 records broad secret inheritance and the required named-secret contract.
resolution: Replace secrets: inherit with explicit named secrets and regression checks.
notes: High severity because unnecessary credentials were exposed to a called workflow boundary.

title: Documented MVP lacked executable shared fixture oracle and canonical result receiver
expected_behavior: The organization-owned v2 baseline provides an authenticated result receiver plus executable TC-MVP-CI-001 inputs and expected outputs.
observed_behavior: Those organization-owned dependencies were identified as blockers to the documented next MVP.
root_cause: Architecture and contract direction had advanced ahead of executable integration assets.
evidence: Issue #113 explicitly identifies the receiver and complete executable fixture/expected-result release as current blockers.
resolution: Implement the canonical receiver and complete no-real-effects shared fixture release.
notes: Classified as verification type because the missing shared oracle prevented conformance proof; receiver implementation was also missing.

title: Reusable consulting operating-system assets were owned by Slugger
expected_behavior: Reusable consulting methods and assets have one authoritative home in consulting-playbook.
observed_behavior: Slugger contained reusable consulting service, intake, assessment, evidence, report, roadmap, proposal, case-study, and knowledge-base assets.

evidence: Issue #112 defines the ownership separation and removal of Slugger consulting/** after migration.
resolution: Consolidate reusable assets into consulting-playbook and remove duplicate active ownership from Slugger.

title: PR #39 made actionlint mandatory before runner behavior was proven
expected_behavior: New CI validation passes on the supported GitHub runner when repository workflows satisfy intended policy.
observed_behavior: Bare actionlint automatically invoked runner ShellCheck and failed the new CI/target validation path; the first fix did not fully stabilize runner-dependent behavior.
root_cause: The PR enabled a new mandatory validator without reproducing its hosted-runner integration behavior in the authoring environment.
evidence: PR #39 review discussion identified SC2046 and subsequent CI failure; follow-up disabled runner-dependent ShellCheck integration for deterministic actionlint.
resolution: Use deterministic actionlint configuration and add regression coverage.

title: Issue-sync checkout persisted GitHub credentials
expected_behavior: All supported checkout steps explicitly disable credential persistence under the repository least-privilege policy.
observed_behavior: sync-slugger-issues.yml checkout persisted the workflow token.
root_cause: Security invariant was not enforced consistently across every workflow checkout step.
evidence: PR #39 follow-up states CI exposed the unsafe checkout and adds repository-wide regression coverage.
resolution: Set persist-credentials: false and enforce it across all workflows.
notes: High severity because a workflow credential remained available to later git commands beyond the intended checkout boundary.

title: PR #39 enabled Ruff CI while existing code violated the enforced rules

expected_behavior: The immutable compatibility unit can validate at least one enabled target using an immutable published adapter reference.
observed_behavior: At c6090e5 the registry stores every target workflow at @main while the router rejects enabled targets unless the workflow ref matches codex-adapter-vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; no core target publishes such a tag.
root_cause: Registry release construction and validation established mutually unsatisfied activation prerequisites.
evidence: config/codex-repositories.json and scripts/codex_router.py at c6090e5; repository tag inventories reviewed 2026-08-13.
resolution: Preserve c6090e5 as historical and publish a corrected immutable compatibility baseline with validated adapter tags.
notes: High severity because issue #117 cannot enable any target without failing the baseline's own validation. The approved recovery is a compatibility repair rather than an activation-only repin.

title: Router dispatch transport and target workflow triggers are incompatible
expected_behavior: The router can invoke the one supported target entry point with the canonical two-input contract.
observed_behavior: The router uses gh workflow run while portfolio-tasks, consulting-playbook, and Slugger expose codex-execute.yml only through workflow_call; control-plane verification simultaneously expects workflow_dispatch plus obsolete inputs.
root_cause: The architecture and executable verification encoded incompatible transport interpretations for dynamic routing.
evidence: .github/scripts/codex_router.py; scripts/verify_target_workflows.py; target codex-execute.yml files; GitHub workflow-dispatch contract.
resolution: Standardize the dynamic MVP target entry point on workflow_dispatch with exactly execution_input_json and concurrency_group and align all validation/docs.
notes: High severity because the router cannot start three target workflows. This is an AI-correct/specification-wrong candidate: target implementations followed workflow_call-oriented local documents while the router implemented dynamic dispatch.

title: Canonical result receiver contract crosses the trust boundary inconsistently
expected_behavior: All targets use one immutable receiver contract and the organization control plane owns trusted-author policy; targets provide only a narrowly scoped delivery credential.
observed_behavior: Three target calls omit the c6090e5 receiver's required CODEX_TRUSTED_JOURNAL_AUTHORS secret, while the .github target pins an older receiver; requiring target-supplied trust policy also assigns authorization policy to the caller boundary.
root_cause: Receiver evolution and target updates were not migrated as one compatibility unit, and trust-policy ownership was placed in a target-supplied secret.
evidence: .github/workflows/codex-result-receiver.yml at c6090e5 and all four target receiver call sites.
resolution: Move trusted-author policy to immutable .github-owned configuration, converge on one receiver interface, and repin through the corrected baseline.
notes: High severity because invalid reusable-workflow calls prevent result delivery and the current secret boundary permits caller-controlled trust policy.

title: Closed conformance work produced false activation assurance
expected_behavior: Issue #116 closes only after each real adapter runs the complete organization-owned TC-MVP-CI-001 oracle against the exact baseline with explicit no-real-effects evidence.
observed_behavior: Organization compatibility validation passes with every target disabled and reports no tested targets; portfolio marks activation evidence insufficient; consulting runs a 2.2.0 26-case local fixture instead of the canonical 2.3.0 29-scenario oracle; Slugger tests vendored schemas that differ from c6090e5.
root_cause: The verification design treated skipped or repository-defined checks as sufficient shared-oracle conformance and completion review did not enforce the issue's evidence criteria.
evidence: Repository conformance reports and fixtures; control-plane compatibility verifier output; open conformance PRs #42/#131/#21/#107.
resolution: Make skipped targets non-acceptance evidence, execute the exact shared oracle through each adapter, and publish explicit activation_evidence_sufficient results.
notes: High severity because a green gate and closed dependency could authorize activation without testing any compatible target.

title: portfolio-tasks target adapter diverges from canonical input and result schemas
expected_behavior: The portfolio target validates the mapping-form registry correctly and emits complete canonical execution-result/v2 fields and enums.
observed_behavior: Registry lookup iterates mapping values as though entries contained a repository field; result construction omits required lifecycle timestamps, uses noncanonical failure/status values, and the receiver call is incomplete.
root_cause: The repository-local adapter implemented local assumptions instead of validating its producer and result builder against the exact shared schemas.
evidence: Merged portfolio PR #136; exact canonical target adapter and schemas; 29/29 TC-MVP-CI-001 scenarios; 22 real-adapter invocations; ten prohibited-effect counters at zero.
resolution: Replaced the divergent target path with the canonical two-input adapter and exact shared schema and fixture identities.
notes: Resolved by merged PR #136. Immutable tags receiver verification credentials and activation remain separate gates.

title: consulting-playbook target adapter and conformance fixture diverge from the canonical route
expected_behavior: The consulting target accepts the router's canonical payload/branch identity, emits execution-result/v2, and proves all canonical scenarios.
observed_behavior: The target requires local task_id/project_component semantics and a consulting-codex branch while the router derives codex branches; it emits a local result shape, exposes only workflow_call, omits a receiver secret, and its report passes 26 local 2.2.0 cases rather than 29 canonical 2.3.0 scenarios.
root_cause: Issue #114 implementation and local tests encoded a repository-defined compatibility model instead of executing the exact organization oracle end to end.
evidence: Merged consulting PR #25 and green replacement conformance run 31857176623; 29/29 scenarios; 22 real-adapter invocations; ten prohibited-effect counters at zero.
resolution: Replaced the local workflow and oracle fork with the canonical two-input adapter receiver boundary and exact shared evidence pin.
notes: Resolved at the repository target layer. Immutable tags receiver verification credentials and activation remain separate gates.

title: Slugger target adapter validates obsolete vendored contract shapes
expected_behavior: Slugger consumes the exact immutable execution-input/result schemas and produces canonical enums and fields through the dispatchable target interface.
observed_behavior: Slugger validates old nested mode/target/source/task payloads and old result fields/statuses; vendored schema blob identities differ from c6090e5, the workflow is workflow_call-only, and the receiver call is incomplete.
root_cause: The local conformance suite treated copied historical schemas as authority instead of consuming the immutable organization baseline.
evidence: Merged Slugger PR #108 plus corrective PR #111; current main passes the complete 29-scenario oracle with 22 real-adapter invocations and ten prohibited-effect counters at zero; adapter revision sha256:9dc5c57580741f60d3391436d1dcae09e4eaa3b7c1449988f2a98acdfbac3df8; report SHA-256 e7c418f93dd3d74a24911e05cbd41a4a75341470de597b96476d1cabd9e46357; green CI run 32539564318.
resolution: Merged the canonical two-input target, exact v2 schemas and fixture oracle, organization receiver boundary, and final synchronized conformance pin/report.
notes: Resolved at the repository target layer by PRs #108 and #111. Immutable tag, registry binding, receiver verification, credentials, and activation remain separate gates.

title: portfolio-tasks source routing lacks the reusable router permission set
expected_behavior: The source workflow grants the least-privilege permissions required by the pinned reusable router and starts a job for an eligible request.
observed_behavior: Recent route-approved-task runs fail during workflow startup with zero jobs; the caller grants contents:read and issues:write while the called router requests actions:read, which a reusable workflow cannot elevate.
root_cause: Caller and called-workflow permission requirements were not validated together at the GitHub Actions boundary.
evidence: Merged portfolio PR #136 adds the reusable router actions:read permission and repository regression coverage.
resolution: Added the least-privilege caller permission and validated the corrected source workflow in the merged recovery change.
notes: Resolved by merged PR #136; live target dispatch remains disabled and was not used as resolution evidence.

title: Conformance report was required to predict its containing commit SHA
expected_behavior: Target evidence is constructible before the final commit exists and is later bound independently to the immutable adapter tag commit and report digest.
observed_behavior: The merged verifier required report.adapter_revision to equal registry.adapter_commit_sha while the report itself had to be committed at that adapter ref; writing a commit SHA into a file changes the tree and therefore changes the commit SHA.
root_cause: The evidence model conflated a pre-commit content identity with the post-commit Git object identity and lacked a release-construction proof for the required artifact.
evidence: Merged .github PR #46; ADR-015; config/mvp-conformance-pin.json; complete 29-scenario zero-effect report.
resolution: Use a canonical non-recursive pin over exact compatibility and target file identities; put that pin revision in the report; separately verify the adapter tag-to-commit binding and report SHA-256; reject self-including pins and reports.
notes: Resolved by merged PR #46. The evidence model is constructible; adapter tags, the final compatibility release, and activation remain separately gated.

title: Compatibility verifier inferred idempotency from workflow keywords
expected_behavior: Compatibility accepts idempotency only when the complete shared oracle executes the exact adapter and harness blobs bound by the conformance pin.
observed_behavior: The live verifier searched the thin workflow wrapper for words such as preflight, ownership marker, create-race, and duplicate-reused even though behavior lived in a separately pinned adapter; comments could pass and a valid wrapper without them could fail.
root_cause: Verification used a syntactic proxy at the transport layer after execution behavior moved behind a pinned adapter seam.
evidence: Merged .github PR #47; executable verifier regressions; complete pinned-adapter oracle; green AI-SDLC Contract Tests and AI-SDLC Target Compatibility.
resolution: Restricted static verification to the transport interface and required the exact pinned adapter plus complete zero-effect oracle for behavioral acceptance.
notes: Resolved by merged .github PR #47. No target, tag, receiver identity, release, or activation was created.

title: Target preflight inferred branch ownership from pull requests
expected_behavior: Before Codex, target preflight independently observes the deterministic branch and every pull request; any disagreement fails ambiguous-rejected without executor or publication effects.
observed_behavior: The merged adapter queried pull requests by head branch but never queried branch existence. An orphaned branch produced an empty PR list and could rerun Codex before the later non-force push failed.
root_cause: The dependency-injected ownership seam modeled only pull requests and incorrectly treated their absence as proof that the branch was absent.
evidence: Merged .github PR #47 and consulting-playbook PR #25; both adapters observe canonical branch plus all PR state before Codex and after create races; 29-case reports pass with zero effects.
resolution: Made branch existence and pull-request ownership one preflight observation; rejected disagreement before Codex and repeated the observation after create races.
notes: Resolved in the central and first consumer adapters. The portfolio recovery candidate applies the same accepted rule; all targets remain disabled.

title: portfolio-tasks source could not construct canonical task-contract/v2
expected_behavior: The source emits exactly one schema-valid task-contract/v2 object whose safe task identity binds every authoritative routing field and current human approval.
observed_behavior: task_id contained owner/repository#issue@digest characters forbidden by the schema; construction omitted risk, scope, and created_by; arbitrary material fields were merged; issue-form values could normalize to unsupported task types.
root_cause: The repository-local producer and issue-form vocabulary were tested against local assumptions instead of the exact shared task schema, and task identity hashed only a subset of routing authority.
evidence: Merged portfolio PR #136; exact task-contract/v2 producer validation; schema-safe identity binds material plus target mode executor dependencies and sensitivity; 114 repository tests pass.
resolution: Constructed and validated the exact closed task object with explicit human-form mappings and authority-complete identity.
notes: Resolved by merged PR #136. Target activation and live execution remain separate gates.

title: portfolio-tasks result projection bypassed the corrected receiver transport
expected_behavior: The target gives only a result-delivery token to the organization receiver; the receiver validates the canonical v2 admission binding and forwards an authenticated bounded repository_dispatch that the source revalidates and projects idempotently.
observed_behavior: The target directly invoked a source workflow_call with a target-held PORTFOLIO_RESULT_TOKEN; the source journal used the obsolete text marker rather than ai-sdlc-admission:v2 JSON and expected result fields outside the corrected canonical result shape.
root_cause: Target and source projection were coupled before receiver trust and forwarding ownership were corrected, while local tests asserted the obsolete closed loop instead of the organization receiver interface.
evidence: Merged portfolio PR #136; exact v2 admission journal; organization receiver repository_dispatch consumer; replay conflict quarantine and receiver allowlist tests.
resolution: Removed direct target-to-source invocation and source token; source projection now accepts only the bounded authenticated receiver event and revalidates schema and admission identity.
notes: Resolved by merged PR #136. Live receiver verification credentials and activation remain separate release gates.

title: Slugger publication token was exposed in Git process arguments
expected_behavior: Publication credentials are supplied only to the narrow publication subprocess and never appear in command arguments remote URLs helper files results or logs.
observed_behavior: The former publisher constructed an authenticated remote URL containing the publication token and passed it to git push; its redaction pattern also did not cover github_pat_ tokens.
root_cause: The publication implementation optimized for a self-contained authenticated URL and relied on incomplete output redaction instead of preventing credential placement in observable process arguments.
evidence: Merged Slugger PR #108 and current main use an anonymous HTTPS remote, secret-free askpass helper, publication-only credential environment, suppressed push output, and sanitized external failures; focused regressions and green CI run 32539564318 confirm the corrected boundary.
resolution: Removed token-bearing Git remote construction and separated anonymous discovery from the narrowly credentialed publication subprocess.
notes: Resolved by merged PR #108 and revalidated after PR #111. No credential value was captured or published; live credential configuration remains a separate release gate.

title: Slugger recovery merge left conformance pin and report out of sync
expected_behavior: Any change to a target file bound by the non-recursive conformance pin atomically regenerates the exact target blob identity, adapter revision, and committed report before merge.
observed_behavior: The final PR #108 head changed the adapter blob while retaining an older target-file blob identity and adapter revision in the pin and report; CI run 32506770178 failed conformance validation.
root_cause: The final adapter change and its derived evidence were not treated as one atomic change, and the recovery branch merged without a passing check on its final head.
evidence: PR #111 synchronized scripts/codex_target_adapter.py blob a590cc98b48cb29defd22d303ec7d45a013e5ea8, adapter revision sha256:9dc5c57580741f60d3391436d1dcae09e4eaa3b7c1449988f2a98acdfbac3df8, and the checked-in report; replacement CI run 32539564318 passed.
resolution: Regenerated the canonical pin and report from the exact final target blobs and required the corrected evidence to pass CI before immutable tagging.
notes: Detected before immutable tag publication or target activation. Prevention requires pin/report regeneration whenever a bound target blob changes and a green check on the exact final head.

title: Portfolio and Slugger conformance pins omitted the executed harness
expected_behavior: Every immutable target evidence pin binds the exact report-producing harness and every organization-required minimum evidence file.
observed_behavior: Both 2.3.1 reports were locally green but their pins omitted scripts/run_tc_mvp_ci_001.py; the independent live verifier rejected both tags.
root_cause: The target-local generator and validator shared an incomplete required-file set, so local consistency checks could not detect that the executed harness identity was absent.
evidence: New immutable 2.3.2 tags bind the harness. Issue #135 checkpoint https://github.com/Young-Consultations/portfolio-tasks/issues/135#issuecomment-5382561301 records live compatibility verification passing for portfolio report SHA-256 9baf2c58d8e0ea055e01eee686610468ed739ae41768140d1e1cf2685092bba1 and Slugger report SHA-256 8283c78bc9dcea9c2424d0ca250ff6031abecd68495692dd809ee03e06060f3c; the exact successful Actions run URL is not preserved in this ledger entry.
resolution: Added the harness to each target pin and regression minimum set, regenerated revisions and reports, preserved 2.3.1 tags, and recorded new 2.3.2 evidence bindings.
notes: High severity because incomplete evidence escaped repository and PR checks into immutable published adapter tags and could have allowed release or activation acceptance without binding the executable harness that generated the report. Rework avoided estimate assumes prevention of post-activation emergency retag plus verifier/release reconciliation across two repositories at ~2 hours each (4 total). All targets stayed disabled; no credential, route, merge, deployment, or production action occurred.

title: PR #32 workflow edit invalidated its conformance pin and report
expected_behavior: Any change to a target file bound by the non-recursive conformance pin atomically regenerates the exact target blob identity, adapter revision, and committed report before merge.
observed_behavior: PR #32 changed .github/workflows/codex-execute.yml while retaining the prior workflow blob identity and adapter revision in the pin/report; exact-head Immutable MVP conformance failed validate_pin.
root_cause: The workflow change was treated as comment-only documentation even though the workflow file is cryptographically bound into target conformance evidence, repeating the prevention failure recorded in DEF-0026.
evidence: PR #32 exact-head conformance failed with conformance pin is invalid. Draft PR #33 recalculates the workflow blob to 8e93f377718587b79a4806947bb6dffed7fdd323 and adapter revision to sha256:609201fc28481fa67d39f63fa089c1b4ab064291fbcea634c578dfc4d58acd00; its workflow has not yet produced a passing job.
resolution: Merge the #33 repair into the #32 branch and require Immutable MVP conformance to pass on the exact final #32 head before main.
notes: Medium severity because the recurrence blocks trustworthy merge evidence but was detected before immutable tagging, activation, credential use, dispatch, or production effects. This is a new defect instance rather than reopening DEF-0026 because it recurred in a different repository after the prevention rule already existed.

title: PR #32 recovery documentation overstated evidence traceability and release scope
expected_behavior: Recovery documentation distinguishes direct workflow evidence from recorded verification attestations, describes the full control-plane recovery scope, and uses current registry status.
observed_behavior: The journal claimed successful live verification while linking only the failed run, described the control-plane recovery as only affected registry-record updates even though PR #52 also changed release metadata and receiver/smoke pins, and NextMVP described the registry binding as eventual after publication.

title: 3.0.2 source cutover would strand missing-result reconciliation
expected_behavior: After source cutover, operator-authorized missing-result reconciliation accepts the explicitly reviewed current 3.0.2 admissions while preserving the existing 3.0.1 admission identity for #159; unsupported releases fail closed and operators cannot choose the accepted release set.
observed_behavior: Portfolio PR #162 moved new source admissions to ai-sdlc-v3.0.2 while reconcile-missing-result.yml remained hard-coded to ai-sdlc-v3.0.1 and admission_binding required exact release equality. Any new 3.0.2 delivery that failed or timed out without a terminal result would remain queued because the authorized recovery workflow would reject its admission.
root_cause: The source cutover treated #159's required 3.0.1 admission preservation as a single-release reconciliation pin rather than as a bounded compatibility requirement spanning the existing 3.0.1 recovery delivery and new 3.0.2 admissions.
evidence: Codex review https://github.com/Young-Consultations/portfolio-tasks/pull/162#discussion_r4139089972 first identified the recovery gap; Copilot review https://github.com/Young-Consultations/portfolio-tasks/pull/162#discussion_r4139914964 independently confirmed that current 3.0.2 admissions would be unrecoverable.
resolution: Resolved before source activation by loading the immutable 3.0.2 trust policy and accepting only the static reviewed admission-release set {ai-sdlc-v3.0.1, ai-sdlc-v3.0.2}. Tests now prove both legacy #159 and current 3.0.2 reconciliation while 2.4.5 remains rejected. Portfolio requirements/interface docs, release record, PR description, and AI_CONTEXT were updated to the resolved rule.
notes: High severity because without the repair a post-cutover failed or timed-out 3.0.2 delivery could become operationally stranded after admission, recreating the missing-result recovery class that DEF-0067 repaired. Detection occurred before merge/activation, so no production delivery was affected. No separate Engineering Journal entry is required because this extends the already-resolved versioned recovery/compatibility principle rather than introducing a new architectural concept.

title: 3.0.2 reconciliation test assertion failed repository format gate
expected_behavior: Source-cutover regression tests satisfy the repository's required ruff formatting gate so functional reconciliation tests can execute.
observed_behavior: Portfolio PR #162 CI run 36655046230 stopped at ruff format --check because the newly added ACCEPTED_CONTROL_PLANE_RELEASES_JSON assertion was split across lines in a form ruff would reformat; pytest and later validation steps were skipped.

evidence: CI job 109697463641 reported exactly one formatting difference in tests/test_workflow_contract.py and exited before pytest. actionlint passed independently.

notes: Low severity because the failure was confined to pre-merge formatting validation and prevented later tests from running; no runtime or production effect occurred. No Engineering Journal or AI_CONTEXT update is warranted.

title: 3.0.2 router rejects preserved predecessor admission on authorized redelivery
expected_behavior: An authorized unchanged retry preserves the original trusted admission evidence for the logical delivery, validates immutable delivery/source/target/contract identity, and dispatches only when the current target-bound immutable policy explicitly permits that predecessor admission release.
observed_behavior: After successful #159 reconciliation on portfolio run 36666315992, the source retained its single durable ai-sdlc-v3.0.1 admission and cleared status:queued. Published ai-sdlc-v3.0.2 router code would regenerate a 3.0.2 admission binding and reject the existing 3.0.1 binding as conflicting before target dispatch, making the documented recovery path impossible.
root_cause: Router retry logic equated same logical delivery with exact equality to a newly generated current-release admission binding. That incorrectly treated original release/activation evidence as retry-generated state instead of durable evidence belonging to the admitted delivery.
evidence: Successful reconciliation run 36666315992 left #159 open without status:queued and added a second reconciliation marker for target run 36480321187 while preserving the original 3.0.1 admission. Inspection of immutable 3.0.2 scripts/codex_router.py showed the subsequent unchanged reapproval would compare that binding against newly generated 3.0.2 release/activation evidence and reject it. Published 3.0.2 release/acceptance docs explicitly require the original admission to be preserved.
resolution: Repair in progress under .github #103 / PR #104. Resolved design: registry idempotency policy declares target-bound reusable_admission_releases; router may reuse exactly one router-owned predecessor admission only when core contract/delivery/correlation/source/target identity matches and the predecessor release is explicitly allowed. Ambiguous, unsupported, malformed, or conflicting admissions fail closed. A new immutable PATCH release and target adapter are required before #159 may be reauthorized.
notes: High severity because the published recovery procedure cannot reach the corrected target after source cutover, blocking REAL acceptance and potentially any cross-release retry of an existing durable delivery. The failure is fail-closed before Codex, so no cost-bearing execution or false source projection occurred. AI_CONTEXT must be updated after the resolved policy is incorporated into the authoritative control-plane release. Engineering Journal entry required because this exposes a reusable cross-release idempotency principle.

title: Cross-release admission repair could duplicate dispatch during concurrent marker creation
expected_behavior: Router admission creation re-reads the source journal after POST and proves exactly one created marker with no concurrent router-owned marker before dispatch; create races fail closed so at most one attempt can proceed.
observed_behavior: PR #104 read existing admissions before POST and made its ambiguity decision from that stale snapshot. Two concurrent attempts could both observe no admission, each POST a marker, and both dispatch.
root_cause: The repair added cross-release admission reuse without carrying the existing create-race requery requirement through the admission-journal write boundary.
evidence: Copilot review discussion https://github.com/Young-Consultations/.github/pull/104#discussion_r4140702992 identified that the pre-POST snapshot could miss concurrently created admissions. The repair now preserves the pre-create snapshot, POSTs only to establish current router identity, re-queries, proves its own posted marker, and rejects any new concurrent router-owned marker before dispatch.
resolution: Resolved on PR #104 and verified by exact-head Contract Tests 36669273526, Target Compatibility 36669273501, and TC-MVP-E2E-001 36669273505.
notes: High severity because duplicate dispatch can create duplicate cost-bearing target attempts despite the registry's create-race/idempotency policy. The defect was caught before merge or REAL retry. Detection_method is blank because the first sufficient evidence came from Copilot review, which is outside the controlled taxonomy.

title: Reusable admission policy validation could crash on unhashable values
expected_behavior: Router and compatibility verifier validate every reusable-admission policy element as a release string before duplicate detection so malformed JSON always produces the documented structured fail-closed rejection.
observed_behavior: Both router and verifier constructed set(reusable_admission_releases) before validating element types. A malformed list containing an object or array raised TypeError and escaped the structured rejection/CompatibilityError contract.
root_cause: Validation order assumed policy entries were hashable before validating their type and format.
evidence: Copilot discussions https://github.com/Young-Consultations/.github/pull/104#discussion_r4140703052 and r4140703111 first identified the malformed-policy crash; Codex discussion r4140745943 independently confirmed it. Regression tests now cover unhashable entries in both router and verifier validation paths.
resolution: Resolved on PR #104 and verified by exact-head Contract Tests 36669273526, Target Compatibility 36669273501, and TC-MVP-E2E-001 36669273505.
notes: Medium severity because malformed policy could crash verification or emit an unstructured router failure rather than the intended governed rejection. No production policy was malformed.

title: Reusable admission releases were not checked against pinned receiver compatibility
expected_behavior: Target compatibility verifies that every cross-release admission allowed by router idempotency policy is accepted by the exact immutable receiver bundle pinned by that target before the target is considered compatible.
observed_behavior: PR #104 initially validated only reusable_admission_releases syntax. The registry listed ai-sdlc-v3.0.3 while the pinned 3.0.2 receiver accepted only 3.0.1 and 3.0.2, so verification could pass a composition that would dispatch work and reject the result afterward.
root_cause: The verifier discarded receiver compatibility-policy contents after validating their shape, so it could not compare the router's reusable-admission set with the receiver allowlist.
evidence: Copilot review discussion https://github.com/Young-Consultations/.github/pull/104#discussion_r4140703075 identified that the router reuse policy could exceed the pinned receiver allowlist. The repair removes premature 3.0.3 reuse, returns the validated receiver allowlist from bundle verification, and requires the router reuse set to be a subset in both normal and release-aware target verification.
resolution: Resolved on PR #104 and verified by exact-head Contract Tests 36669273526, Target Compatibility 36669273501, and TC-MVP-E2E-001 36669273505.
notes: High severity because an invalid composition could pass preflight, permit cost-bearing target work, and only then have the receiver reject the result. The repair moves the incompatibility back before execution. Detection_method is blank because Copilot first produced sufficient evidence.

title: Cross-release allowlist regressed same-release admission retry
expected_behavior: An exact existing admission binding from the same control-plane release remains reusable regardless of whether cross-release predecessor reuse is configured; the reusable-admission allowlist is consulted only when the existing admission release differs from the current binding.
observed_behavior: PR #104 initially required every existing admission release to appear in reusable_admission_releases. Targets with an empty cross-release list would therefore reject an unchanged same-release retry if later enabled.
root_cause: The new predecessor compatibility list was applied to all admission reuse rather than only cross-release reuse.
evidence: Codex review discussion https://github.com/Young-Consultations/.github/pull/104#discussion_r4140745939 identified that empty cross-release allowlists would break the pre-existing same-release idempotency path. The router now accepts exact prior-binding equality before consulting cross-release compatibility and tests a target with an empty reuse list.
resolution: Resolved on PR #104 and verified by exact-head Contract Tests 36669273526, Target Compatibility 36669273501, and TC-MVP-E2E-001 36669273505.
notes: Medium severity because the regression would fail closed but could strand valid redelivery for currently disabled targets after future activation. Existing enabled consulting cross-release behavior was the immediate focus, so the broader same-release regression was caught only at review.

title: Malformed-policy regression test inherited Actions output transport
expected_behavior: Router subprocess tests that assert stdout structured outputs remove GITHUB_OUTPUT from the child environment so output transport matches the test oracle.
observed_behavior: TC-MVP-E2E-001 run 36669170838 failed one router test because the child validate-registry process inherited GitHub's GITHUB_OUTPUT and correctly wrote failure_category there, while the test incorrectly expected failure_category on stdout.
root_cause: The new test did not isolate its subprocess transport from the GitHub Actions environment even though the existing router test harness deliberately removes GITHUB_OUTPUT when asserting stdout.
evidence: Run 36669170838 executed 90 selected tests; 89 passed and only test_registry_rejects_unhashable_reusable_admission_release_policy failed because failure_category was routed to GITHUB_OUTPUT rather than stdout. Router rejection itself occurred correctly and no SIM/real effects ran.
resolution: Resolved by filtering GITHUB_OUTPUT from the child subprocess environment and verified by exact-head Contract Tests 36669273526, Target Compatibility 36669273501, and TC-MVP-E2E-001 36669273505.
notes: Low severity because the failure was confined to the new pre-merge regression test and did not indicate runtime behavior failure.

title: Consulting target authority retained stale pre-3.0.2 runtime state
expected_behavior: Target requirements, interface architecture, and AI_CONTEXT identify published ai-sdlc-v3.0.2 and codex-adapter-v3.0.2 as current runtime while distinguishing the unpublished 3.0.3 corrective candidate and its unresolved REAL acceptance.
observed_behavior: During construction of the 3.0.3 target candidate, authoritative target documents still described ai-sdlc-v3.0.1/codex-adapter-v3.0.0 or even 2.4.5 as current and described 3.0.2 or 3.0.0 as unpublished future candidates, despite successful 3.0.2 publication, deployed preflights, and portfolio source adoption.
root_cause: Prior release/cutover work synchronized organization and portfolio authority but did not update the consulting target's full current-state documentation set after 3.0.2 adoption.
evidence: Live published control-plane and target evidence establish 3.0.2 as current: ai-sdlc-v3.0.2, codex-adapter-v3.0.2 at 3bde0dc760088b9af21454a0f70ed498dae043a7, Runtime Preflight 36640642872, REAL preflight 36640734704, and merged portfolio source adoption PR #162. The target documents contradicted that state. Codex review discussion https://github.com/Young-Consultations/consulting-playbook/pull/80#discussion_r4145245739 then identified a remaining contradictory current-runtime declaration in the normative NextMVP authority header.
resolution: Resolved on consulting-playbook PR #80 by updating the NextMVP authority header and operational sections, InterfaceArchitecture, and AI_CONTEXT to the verified 3.0.2 runtime, preserving historical evidence, and recording 3.0.3 only as the pre-publication DEF-0086 candidate.
notes: Medium severity because stale authoritative runtime identity could misdirect release, rollback, and acceptance work but did not change executable behavior. AI_CONTEXT required correction because the architectural decision and current published state are already resolved. Phase-dependent metrics are intentionally blank because the stale state originated during a prior release/cutover lifecycle and was detected during a later 3.0.3 implementation cycle; forcing those into one ordered lifecycle would produce an invalid negative escape distance. No separate Engineering Journal entry is warranted.

title: New defect rows used uncontrolled taxonomy values and invalid escape-distance classification
expected_behavior: Every defect-ledger row uses only controlled taxonomy values, and phase-dependent metrics are recorded only when origin and detection phases belong to a supportable ordered lifecycle.

evidence: Copilot review discussion https://github.com/Young-Consultations/consulting-playbook/pull/79#discussion_r4145938428 identified both the uncontrolled types and the invalid phase/escape-distance relationship.

All affected rows remain valid 31-column CSV.
notes: Low severity because the defect affected taxonomy and learning metrics rather than runtime behavior, and it was caught before merge. Detection_method is blank because the first sufficient evidence came from Copilot review, which is outside the controlled detection-method taxonomy. No Engineering Journal or AI_CONTEXT update is warranted.

title: 3.0.3 candidate registry conformance binding violated the closed evidence schema
expected_behavior: The target registry conformance object contains only the controlled conformance fields; adapter revision remains in the immutable target report/pin and release documentation while the registry separately binds adapter tag/commit and report digest.
observed_behavior: During 3.0.3 central candidate wiring, the consulting registry conformance object was given an extra adapter_revision key. The closed conformance validator rejected the whole consulting entry as malformed, causing router validation and E2E tests to fail before their intended assertions.
root_cause: The release binding duplicated target report metadata into a closed registry schema that deliberately separates target report contents from registry tag/commit/report-digest bindings.
evidence: Initial 3.0.3 Target Compatibility and E2E candidate runs failed with 'reviewed conformance evidence is missing or malformed'. Inspection of the closed CONFORMANCE_FIELDS contract showed adapter_revision is not a registry field.
resolution: Resolved on PR #104 by removing adapter_revision from config/codex-repositories.json while retaining it in the immutable target conformance report/pin and release documentation. Exact-head Contract Tests 36765536153, Target Compatibility 36765536048, and TC-MVP-E2E-001 36765536222 then passed.
notes: Medium severity because the malformed central registry blocked all routing/candidate verification fail-closed before execution. No production runtime was changed and no Codex call occurred. No Engineering Journal or AI_CONTEXT update is warranted.

title: 3.0.3 bundled receiver regression retained the previous 3.0.2 runtime identity
expected_behavior: The production-policy regression exercises the bundled receiver using the candidate receiver release while proving that the reviewed predecessor 3.0.1 admission remains accepted.
observed_behavior: After the bundled compatibility policy advanced to receiver_release ai-sdlc-v3.0.3, the regression still invoked receive with runtime identity ai-sdlc-v3.0.2, so it failed with 'receiver release does not match immutable compatibility policy' rather than testing predecessor admission compatibility.
root_cause: The release candidate advanced the production policy identity without advancing the corresponding test runtime identity.
evidence: Initial 3.0.3 E2E candidate tests failed test_bundled_3_0_2_policy_accepts_3_0_1_admission because the runtime release no longer matched the bundled policy. The repair renamed/rebound the test to the 3.0.3 bundle while preserving the 3.0.1 admission assertion.
resolution: Resolved before candidate merge and verified by exact-head Contract Tests 36765536153 and TC-MVP-E2E-001 36765536222.
notes: Low severity because the defect was confined to candidate regression identity and failed closed during CI; runtime compatibility policy itself was correct.

title: 3.0.3 candidate lifecycle test skipped the publishable-gate rejection
expected_behavior: The 3.0.3 lifecycle test proves both that candidate readiness succeeds for tag_published false/tag_commit_sha null and that the same unpublished state fails the publishable gate.
observed_behavior: The first 3.0.3 test conversion called validate_release(require_candidate_ready=True) twice, pairing the second call with the expected publishable-release failure text. It therefore did not exercise require_publishable=True.
root_cause: The published-to-candidate test rewrite changed expected state but duplicated the candidate gate invocation instead of retaining opposite candidate/publication assertions.
evidence: Static candidate audit of tests/test_release_lifecycle.py found the duplicate candidate gate before the final candidate CI completed.
resolution: Resolved by restoring require_publishable=True for the negative publication assertion. Exact-head Contract Tests 36765536153 passed.
notes: Low severity because this was an in-progress verification-oracle defect detected before merge, tag, publication, or deployed preflight.

title: 3.0.3 receiver compatibility negative test treated a reviewed release as unsupported
expected_behavior: The receiver allowlist negative regression selects a release outside the candidate's reviewed compatibility set so it continues proving that excess router reuse policy is rejected.
observed_behavior: After the 3.0.3 receiver candidate intentionally expanded accepted_admission_releases to include ai-sdlc-v3.0.3, the verifier negative test still used 3.0.3 as the supposedly unsupported reusable admission release. Target Compatibility therefore correctly did not raise CompatibilityError.
root_cause: The test input was not advanced with the compatibility policy and stopped representing the boundary it was intended to test.
evidence: Initial Target Compatibility failed test_receiver_verification_rejects_reuse_outside_receiver_allowlist with 'DID NOT RAISE CompatibilityError' because 3.0.3 was now legitimately accepted.
resolution: Resolved by moving the negative input to unsupported ai-sdlc-v3.0.4. Exact-head Target Compatibility 36765536048 and Contract Tests 36765536153 passed.
notes: Low severity because the compatibility implementation was correct and the obsolete negative test was caught before candidate merge.

title: Control-plane authority retained stale 3.0.1 source-consumer state after 3.0.2 adoption
expected_behavior: Control-plane README, release procedures, acceptance authority, router/interface guidance, and AI_CONTEXT distinguish the published/source-adopted 3.0.2 runtime from the unpublished 3.0.3 DEF-0086 candidate and block #159 until candidate publication/preflights/source repin complete.
observed_behavior: During 3.0.3 candidate preparation, multiple authoritative .github documents still stated that portfolio-tasks consumed 3.0.1 and that 3.0.2 source adoption/preflights were pending even though Runtime Preflight 36640642872, REAL preflight 36640734704, and portfolio PR #162 had already completed.
root_cause: The prior 3.0.2 source cutover updated executable source routing and some authority surfaces but did not synchronize the complete control-plane current-state documentation set before the next release cycle.
evidence: Live source routing on portfolio-tasks main and completed 3.0.2 preflight/cutover evidence contradicted stale current-state text in README, docs/releases.md, TC-MVP-E2E-001, mvp-v2 compatibility guidance, codex-router guidance, and AI_CONTEXT.
resolution: Resolved on PR #104 by synchronizing current source consumption to published 3.0.2, recording #159 reconciliation/DEF-0086 state, and documenting 3.0.3 only as an unpublished candidate. Phase-dependent metrics are intentionally blank because the stale documentation originated in a prior release lifecycle and was discovered during the later 3.0.3 candidate cycle.
notes: Medium severity because stale operator/AI authority could direct release or REAL acceptance work through obsolete gates even though executable routing remained fail-closed. AI_CONTEXT required correction after the verified current-state decision; no separate Engineering Journal entry is warranted.

title: 3.0.3 publication attestation found runtime test still asserting published 3.0.2
expected_behavior: Release lifecycle verification describes the same current release state as the authoritative manifest/runtime record; after 3.0.3 publication attestation the runtime-preflight test asserts published 3.0.3 and the exact immutable tag commit.
observed_behavior: After PR #104 merged and ai-sdlc-v3.0.3 was tagged, release/release-manifest.json and release/current-runtime.json described 3.0.3 candidate state while tests/test_runtime_preflight.py still asserted published ai-sdlc-v3.0.2 at the 3.0.2 commit, contradicting the runtime record it first requires to equal generate_current_runtime.render().
root_cause: The 3.0.3 candidate conversion advanced the generated runtime record and release-specific tests unevenly, leaving a stale published-release oracle in tests/test_runtime_preflight.py; the required candidate gates did not surface that file-level contradiction before merge/tag.
evidence: Tag comparison proved ai-sdlc-v3.0.3 and main were identical at f3229bfa4a06da963cae7c390c6075b4f6c12f7b. Direct inspection then showed release/current-runtime.json at 3.0.3 while tests/test_runtime_preflight.py still asserted 3.0.2. Issue #105 preserves the discrepancy and classification.
notes: Medium severity because the stale oracle could invalidate or confuse publication verification, but executable runtime behavior was unchanged and later deployment/REAL gates remained blocked. The defect should close only after .github PR #106 merges and exact-head publication tests pass. No Engineering Journal or consulting AI_CONTEXT update is warranted.
